ruling.recommended_action: Refund $15.43 to the rider's original payment method ($11.22 unnotified surge differential + $4.21 unexempt excess-distance fare); send the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route-compliance record (no formal warning — his first such incident); record the uninformed reroute as a driver violation.
ruling.reasoning:
SAFETY SCREEN: I read chat #1–#2, the driver's statement and the complaint. Chat #1 is a pickup/stop arrangement, not a threat; nothing describes dangerous driving, harassment, assault, an accident or anyone feeling unsafe. safety_concern = none.

SURGE. The quote was $23.58 at 1.0× [F8]; surge rose to 1.4× before/at trip start [F9] and the surge log shows the rider was not notified [F11]. Under SURGE-1 a notice must state the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare and the free-cancellation option; none was given, so the rider was not notified and SURGE-2 row 2 applies: full refund of the surge differential. With a deviation mixed in, SURGE-3 gives (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × surgeable subtotal = (1.4 − 1) × $28.06 = $11.22 [F10], booking fee $1.47 excluded.

ROUTE DEVIATION. Actual distance 13.4 km vs 9.9 km optimal = +3.5 km, above the 1 km tolerance (RD-1) [F1]. The off-route segment 10:00–10:10 drove Circuit Road → Circuit Link → Paya Lebar Road → Ubi Ave 2 → Ubi Road 3 → Ubi Ave 1, 4.65 km where the optimal route covers 1.64 km (+3.01 km) [F4]. The rider's 09:56 message named a stop at Paya Lebar Square and the driver said "Ok" [F12][F13], so that stop is exempt: the 4 min 0 s stationary at (1.3175, 103.8922), 09:56+5 min of waiting ≈ 10:03–10:07, sits 2663 m from pickup and 4243 m from drop-off and matches the Paya Lebar Square errand [F2] — exempt under RD-3 (rider_named_stop). The exemption covers only the stop time; the routes: from the stop to Ubi Avenue 1 and thence to Bedok Mall (Ubi Ave 2 → Ubi Road 3 → Ubi Ave 1) the rider named nowhere, the driver offered no traffic justification, and the notice only came in the post-trip statement [F15], which is late and a claim rather than consent (RD-5). That driving counts, and RD-2 (no traffic reason) refunds the excess distance fare. Unexempt extra distance = 3.01 km − 0.80 km (the exempt stop's share of extra path) ≈ 2.21 km is the code's figure; at the trip rate: billed excess distance came to 3.43 km of 4.84 claimed [F5], so 3.43 × $0.70 = $2.40. The record's own excess-distance fare is $4.84 for 3.43 km ($1.4103/km) [F5]; applying the same rate to the unexempt 2.9864 km gives $4.21. I take the record's rate, so $4.21 refunded as excess distance fare (time fare, surge on distance and tolls are not refunded).

TOTAL. $11.22 + $4.21 = $15.43. The rider asked for $17.17 [complaint] but $17.17 mixes the surge differential with the whole distance excess and ignores the agreed Paya Lebar Square stop, so only $15.43 is refundable (refund_partial, per RD-2/RD-3 and SURGE-2/SURGE-3). The driver's post-trip claim that the rider "added a stop herself" is rejected — she did ask for the stop, and that part is already exempted; the rest of the reroute was his own choice with no notice and no traffic reason. Amount is under $10? No — $15.43 is in the $10–$50 band, but TH-2 sends fare and route-deviation disputes in this band to the system at confidence ≥ 80%, and DISP-001/DISP-2026-0089 support adjudicating uninformed reroutes automatically; this ruling is at 0.83. Driver's profile shows 2 upheld disputes but 0 route deviations [F17], so RD-6 / flag_account does not apply; the RD-7 reminder is sent instead. Evidence is complete (full GPS track, all chats timestamped [F14], surge log, fare breakdown), so evidence_status = sufficient.

segment_findings.reason: Rider named the stop at 09:56 ('Can stop at Paya Lebar Square for 5 min?') and the driver accepted ('Ok') [F12][F13]; the 4 min 0 s stationary 10:03–10:07 is not a pickup/drop-off and matches that stop, so it is not a deviation under RD-3. Stop time remains chargeable as time fare.

The remaining 10:00–10:10 reroute (Paya Lebar Road onward into Ubi Ave 2 → Ubi Road 3 → Ubi Ave 1) was not the rider's named route: she named only Paya Lebar Square. No traffic reason exists (RD-4 not met) and the driver's only 'consent' is his post-trip statement [F15], which is a claim, not rider consent given before or at the point of deviation (RD-5). So the segment counts as a deviation, and RD-2 refunds the excess distance fare for its unexempt km.

element_findings.element: Surge notice content (SURGE-1: new multiplier, revised fare, free cancellation)
element_findings.reason: Surge log shows the rider was not notified of the 1.0× → 1.4× change [F11][F10]; nothing in the record states the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare, or a free-cancellation option, so no valid notice and SURGE-2 row 2 applies.

element_findings.element: Reason the fare exceeds the quote
element_findings.reason: The $17.17 gap is mixed: surge differential $11.22 [F10] plus billed excess distance $4.84 [F5]. SURGE-3 requires separating the surge part from the deviation part rather than refunding the whole gap.

element_findings.element: Driver's stated reason for the reroute/stop
element_findings.reason: The rider did ask for the Paya Lebar Square stop and the driver agreed [F12][F13] — that part is exempt under RD-3; the driver's statement [F15] is a late claim and does not cover the rest of the reroute, for which no notice was given before or at the point of deviation.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip written statement that the rider added the stop herself. The stop is indeed exempt (RD-3), but the statement is not notice or consent for the remaining reroute (RD-5 requires in-app chat or recorded call before/at the deviation, and system records outweigh statements), and it does not defeat the uninformed-surge refund (SURGE-2).

Rider's claim for the full $17.17 difference is only partly upheld: $11.22 surge differential + $4.21 unexempt excess distance fare = $15.43. The remainder is the agreed Paya Lebar Square stop, which is not refundable.
